classes.name: Z-drug hypnotics
classes.description: Zolpidem IR/ER/SL (Ambien, Ambien CR, Edluar), eszopiclone (Lunesta), zaleplon; ramelteon (Rozerem) and low-dose doxepin (Silenor) may be listed as alternatives.
classes.plainDescription: A bedtime pill for trouble falling or staying asleep.

classes.name: Orexin receptor antagonists
classes.description: Dual orexin receptor antagonists: suvorexant (Belsomra), lemborexant (Dayvigo), daridorexant (Quviviq).
classes.plainDescription: A newer bedtime pill that blocks the brain's wake signal.

classes.name: Benzodiazepines and buspirone for anxiety
classes.description: Benzodiazepines (alprazolam IR/ER, lorazepam, clonazepam, diazepam, chlordiazepoxide, clorazepate) and the non-benzodiazepine anxiolytics buspirone and hydroxyzine as alternatives.
classes.plainDescription: A medicine for anxiety or panic attacks.

preferredAgent.sig: 1 tablet (5 mg) by mouth at bedtime as needed, with at least 7 hours left for sleep. 5 mg is the labeled starting dose for women and adults 65+; men may start at 5 or 10 mg (label dosing).
preferredAgent.plainSig: One small pill at bedtime when needed, only if you can sleep 7 or more hours.

alternatives.note: Preferred, no PA (PDL p.17); melatonin agonist, listed as an alternative in the class description

records.verificationNote: Read PDL p.17 (Central Nervous System, Sedative Hypnotics). Zolpidem IR tablet is Preferred; zolpidem SL and zolpidem IR capsule require PA. Judgment call: 5 mg is the label starting dose for women and the common low dose (no sex or dose restriction printed). Controlled (C-IV): no quantity or day-supply limit printed. Hypnotic benzodiazepines on the same heading (temazepam 7.5 and 22.5 mg, estazolam, triazolam, flurazepam, quazepam, Halcion, Restoril, Doral) require PA, except temazepam 15 and 30 mg which is Preferred; they are outside this class and not listed here.

preferredAgent.sig: 10 mg once, within 30 minutes of bedtime, with at least 7 hours left before waking; may increase to 20 mg (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill at bedtime, only if you can sleep 7 or more hours.

records.preferredRestriction: PA required (PDL p.17). No DC PA criteria form is linked for this heading.
records.verificationNote: Read PDL p.17 (Sedative Hypnotics). All three orexin antagonists (Belsomra, Dayvigo, Quviviq) are in the PA column; none is Preferred. Judgment call: Belsomra chosen as the first-listed and most widely written DORA; the three share identical PDL status. Ramelteon is Preferred but is a melatonin agonist, not a DORA, so it is recorded under the Z-drug class alternatives only. Controlled status not stated on the PDL line.

preferredAgent.sig: Panic disorder: 0.25 mg by mouth twice daily; increase to 1 mg/day (0.5 mg twice daily) after 3 days; max 4 mg/day. Taper to stop (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: Half of a small pill twice a day at first, then a whole pill; do not stop suddenly.

records.verificationNote: Read PDL p.12 (Central Nervous System, Anticonvulsants: First Generation). Clonazepam (generic) is Preferred with no PA; Klonopin and clonazepam ODT require PA. The PDL files clonazepam under anticonvulsants, not anxiety. Alprazolam, lorazepam, oral diazepam, chlordiazepoxide, clorazepate, buspirone and hydroxyzine do not appear on this PDL. The anxiolytic heading is not a PDL class, so those agents are covered on the Medicaid formulary and are not confirmed here. Controlled (C-IV): no quantity or day-supply limit printed. Sig is label dosing for panic disorder, not printed on the PDL.

preferredAgent.sig: 1 tablet (5 mg) by mouth at bedtime as needed, with at least 7 hours left for sleep. 5 mg is the labeled starting dose for women and adults 65+; men may start at 5 or 10 mg (label dosing).

records.verificationNote: Read PDF pp. 70-71, 77-78 (zolpidem IR F, no QL; Ambien CR F PA; Edluar NF PA; eszopiclone and zaleplon F). Zolpidem strength is not printed; 5 mg is the label starting dose for women. Not on the list: Lunesta, Sonata, Rozerem (ramelteon); Silenor (low-dose doxepin tablet) is not listed (doxepin capsules at PDF p. 89 are the depression product, not Silenor). Controlled substance, but no quantity limit is printed, so preferredRestriction is null.

preferredAgent.sig: 25-50 mg once, within 30 minutes of bedtime, with at least 7 hours left before waking (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill at bedtime, only if you can sleep 7 or more hours.

records.verificationNote: Read PDF p. 83 (Orexin Receptor Antagonists section). Quviviq is the only DORA on the list and it is NF PA; no covered DORA is printed. Suvorexant (Belsomra) and lemborexant (Dayvigo) do not appear in the document, so their coverage is unknown and they are not recorded as excluded. Strength not printed on the list; 25 mg is the label starting dose.

records.verificationNote: Read PDF pp.61-62, 77, 162 (formulary pp.59-60, 75, 160). Alprazolam 0.5 mg is Tier 1 with QL 150 tablets per 30 days. Lorazepam, chlordiazepoxide, clorazepate and diazepam are Tier 1 with QL. Clonazepam is Tier 1 with no QL printed. Buspirone is Tier 1 with no flag. Hydroxyzine is Tier 1 with PA and a High Risk Medications flag; the flag's criteria are not printed. Alprazolam ODT and concentrate are the same molecule and not repeated. Xanax, Ativan and Klonopin brands are not listed.
